Publisher XML converted to located text (jats_text), bg-19-5287-2022
pages_convention: XML section and paragraph locators (jats_text); figure-content steps cite the figure plus the printed journal page of the PDF in parentheses. The XML repeats the numbers §4.2.1 and §4.2.2 for two different subsections each, so locators in the LOTOS-EUROS uncertainty subsection carry the heading in parentheses.

entry.evidence: This dataset provides a unique opportunity for the evaluation of different approaches to quantify dry deposition fluxes.

steps.action: Took the 2.5-year TRANC eddy-covariance ΣNr flux and concentration record from the companion paper (Part I) as the measured reference.
steps.quote: Wintjen et al. (2022) presented and analyzed novel flux measurements of Σ N r and several subcomponents

steps.action: Posed the aim: compare four independent methods (TRANC, DEPAC-1D, LOTOS-EUROS, CBT) for the annual ΣNr dry deposition budget at a remote mixed forest.
steps.quote: we provide a comparison of four independent methods for estimating nitrogen dry deposition for a remote mixed forest site

steps.action: Gap-filled the TRANC flux series (41% coverage) in two ways, with DEPAC-1D alone and with MDV plus DEPAC-1D, and propagated gap-filling uncertainty (Eq. 1).
steps.quote: we filled gaps in the TRANC flux data with results from DEPAC-1D and, henceforth, called this dataset TRANC(DEPAC-1D)

steps.action: Computed model expectations: a nested 7x7 km LOTOS-EUROS run with DEPAC and footprint land-use weighting, and a site-driven DEPAC-1D run with measured meteorology and concentrations.
steps.quote: DEPAC-1D used micrometeorological variables and parameters measured at the site to estimate R c and the compensation point of NH 3

steps.action: Estimated lower and upper annual dry deposition from throughfall and bulk deposition with the canopy budget technique, averaging two CBT variants and adding ΔDON.
steps.quote: Adding Δ DON to throughfall DIN or to DIN t reveals a frame of lower and upper estimates of total (wet + dry) nitrogen deposition

steps.action: Compared LOTOS-EUROS concentrations with high-resolution QCL, CL and TRANC concentrations and found NH3 and ΣNr overestimated by a factor of 2 to 3 outside summer.
steps.quote: Except for the summer, modeled half-hourly concentrations of Σ N r were 2 to 3 times higher than the measured values.

steps.action: Checked the NH3 overestimation against independent passive-sampler and DELTA measurements, and checked DELTA-summed ΣNr against TRANC.
steps.quote: The large modeled NH 3 concentrations by LOTOS-EUROS could also not be verified by the observed levels of the passive samplers and the DELTA system.

steps.action: Compared modeled with measured compound contributions (NH3 dominant in the model, NOx in the measurements) and modeled with measured ΣNr deposition velocities; DEPAC-1D vd was 2 to 3 times TRANC in summer.
steps.quote: Particularly during the summer months, an overestimation of v d by DEPAC-1D was observed with respect to TRANC measurements.

steps.action: Split May–September diurnal vd cycles by median temperature, relative humidity, concentration and leaf wetness; the models' enhancement under wet conditions contradicted TRANC.
steps.quote: This behavior was expected based on the models' parameterizations, but it is contradictory to the TRANC measurements.

steps.action: Compared LOTOS-EUROS meteorological inputs with site measurements (temperature, radiation, RH, u*); u* showed a systematic difference (R2 0.43).
steps.quote: In the case of u ∗ , we found a systematic difference, and the seasonal pattern did not agree well

steps.action: Swapped one LOTOS-EUROS input at a time for its measured value in DEPAC-1D spruce runs; the NH3 concentration had by far the largest effect (5.3 kg N ha-1).
steps.quote: Using measured NH 3 concentrations reduced the deposition substantially, by 5.3 kg N ha - 1 , compared to using modeled concentrations.

steps.action: Compared modeled ΣNr fluxes with high-quality TRANC fluxes by month and season: seasonal pattern captured, amplitude overestimated; DEPAC-1D high in summer, LOTOS-EUROS high in spring, autumn and winter.
steps.quote: Models were basically able to capture the seasonal pattern of the Σ N r fluxes well but generally overestimated the measured flux amplitude.

steps.action: Integrated cumulative and annual ΣNr dry deposition for each method: TRANC 4.3 to 4.7, DEPAC-1D 5.8 and LOTOS-EUROS 6.5 kg N ha-1 a-1, with uncertainties.
steps.quote: DEPAC-1D showed 5.8 ± 0.1 kg N ha - 1 a - 1 , and LOTOS-EUROS predicted 6.5 ± 0.3 kg N ha - 1 [...]

steps.action: Compared the two gap-filling strategies on the same TRANC data and found similar budgets.
steps.quote: both gap-filling strategies resulted in similar deposition estimates, showing that the application of MDV as a gap-filling tool is reasonable.

steps.action: Checked all annual estimates against the independent long-term (2010–2018) CBT lower and upper bounds; all fell inside.
steps.quote: All deposition estimates were within the range of long-term lower and upper estimates of the CBT approach

steps.action: Proposed explanations for the mismatches: NH3 emission allocation in the inventory (LOTOS-EUROS), and concentration inputs, micrometeorology and missing exchange pathways in DEPAC (DEPAC-1D).
steps.quote: The predominant role of NH 3 in the modeled concentrations is caused by the emission inventory used in this study.

steps.action: Set the site budgets against the multi-site comparison by Ahrends et al. (2020), noting differences in method and agreement with its minimum estimates.
steps.quote: Since we measured N deposition in a low-polluted environment, the agreement to the minimum dry deposition estimates of Ahrends et al. (2020) seems reasonable.

steps.action: Added local wet-only deposition to obtain total deposition of 11.5 to 14.8 kg N ha-1 a-1 and kept it as within critical loads, supported by cited ecological indicators at the site.
steps.quote: [...] of critical loads, total nitrogen deposition is within the proposed limits.

steps.action: Concluded from the wet/dry contradiction that DEPAC's current NH3 exchange-pathway implementation is not fully suited, pending further investigation.
steps.quote: the current implementation of the NH 3 exchange pathways in DEPAC was not fully suited for predicting NH 3 deposition correctly

steps.action: Excluded the known underestimate of the cuticular NH3 compensation point (Schrader et al., 2016) as the main cause of the flux mismatch at this low-NH3 site.
steps.quote: Thus, this issue could not be the main reason for the difference to flux measurements at our site.

steps.action: Varied z0, d and LAI by ±50% in DEPAC-1D; LAI changed the budget by +18.9% to -27.2% but alone could not explain the overestimation.
steps.quote: An incorrect assessment of the modeled LAI by ± 50 % had a significant influence on the dry deposition.

steps.action: Estimated the bias from using monthly averaged concentrations by comparing LOTOS-EUROS hourly fluxes (A1) with monthly vd times monthly concentration (A2).
steps.quote: we compared monthly averaged fluxes of LOTOS-EUROS (A1) with fluxes calculated by multiplying monthly averaged v d with their monthly concentration averages (A2)

steps.action: Ran LOTOS-EUROS for 2015 at 2x2 km and found concentrations only 2 to 10% lower, excluding grid resolution as the primary cause of the overestimation.
steps.quote: the grid cell resolution of 7 × 7 km 2 is not primarily responsible for the overestimation of concentrations and fluxes

steps.action: Used van der Graaf et al. (2020): MODIS LAI and z0 left site deposition and NH3 nearly unchanged, excluding surface parameters as the explanation.
steps.quote: if LAI and z 0 from MODIS were used, there was almost no change observable in Σ N r dry deposition

steps.action: Kept imprecise spatial and temporal allocation of emission data as the best explanation of the LOTOS-EUROS disagreement.
steps.quote: We assume that the spatially and temporally imprecise allocation of emission data is most responsible for the disagreement to flux measurements.

steps.action: Kept the headline claim that all methods' annual ΣNr dry deposition estimates lie in the same range, within the CBT bounds.
steps.quote: dry deposition estimates of all methods were in the same range, considering uncertainties of measured fluxes and model applications

steps.action: Kept DEPAC-1D, and inferential modeling generally, as a valuable gap-filling tool at sites with prevailing deposition.
steps.quote: DEPAC-1D (and by extension, inferential modeling in general) is a valuable gap-filling tool at sites with prevailing N deposition

tree.answer: ΣNr dry deposition to a remote mixed forest, and model–measurement mismatches in it
Half-hourly fluxes are measured directly (inherited, 41% coverage); annual budgets need gap-filling and inference
Annual dry deposition budget compared across four methods
Rival causes of the mismatch: emission inventory, meteorological inputs, grid resolution, LAI/z0, cuticular compensation point, low-resolution concentrations, missing soil and emission pathways
Partly: input-swap, resolution and LAI tests separate the effects of some rivals
Found, not set: field campaign 2016–2018; conditions stratified by temperature, RH, concentration and leaf wetness
Budgets robust to gap-filling choice and within the CBT range; NH3 overestimation replicated with DELTA and passive samplers
Budgets kept as estimates with uncertainties; emission allocation kept as best explanation; DEPAC wet-condition response contradicted
Not assessed: no review file or discussion supplied

end.claim: Annual ΣNr dry deposition at the Bavarian Forest site was 4.3–4.7 (gap-filled TRANC), 5.8 (DEPAC-1D) and 6.5 (LOTOS-EUROS) kg N ha-1 a-1, all within the CBT range of 3.8–6.7; with wet deposition, total deposition was 11.5–14.8 kg N ha-1 a-1, within critical loads.

decisive_move.sentence: Without gap-filling the 41%-coverage TRANC flux record (DEPAC-1D and MDV) and integrating every method to annual sums, there would be no measured budget against which to set the models and the CBT.

gates.evidence: The campaign aimed to quantify background deposition (§1 ¶5); no hypothesis directed data acquisition, and the fluxes are inherited from Part I. The headline budget faced checks it could have failed (consistency with the independent CBT range, §3.4 ¶3; gap-filling variants, §3.4 ¶2), but no agreement criterion was fixed beforehand. The model expectation of enhanced vd under wet conditions was explicitly tested and contradicted (§3.2.2 ¶4). Nothing was pre-registered.

imports.item: quantum cascade laser NH3 concentration measurement
chemiluminescence detection of NO/NO2 (and TRANC-coupled CLD)
critical load concept for nitrogen effects on ecosystems

novelty_claims.quote: This dataset provides a unique opportunity for the evaluation of different approaches to quantify dry deposition fluxes.
[...] novel measurement techniques are sparse and only available from a few field campaigns

limits: No review file, open discussion or earlier version was supplied, so no review sequence is coded, although the acknowledgements say reviewers' comments improved the paper significantly. The supplement (Figs. S1–S8, Tables S1–S2) was not supplied; steps resting on it (S1 NH3 comparison, S6 input comparison) are coded from the main-text description. The XML repeats the numbers §4.2.1 and §4.2.2 for different subsections; locators are disambiguated by heading. 'Same range' and 'reasonable agreement' are not given a quantitative criterion. Uncertainties are gap-filling uncertainties only; systematic errors are excluded (§2.1 ¶4). Sub-claim statuses: the emission-allocation explanation of the LOTOS-EUROS overestimation is best_explanation (§4.2.2 ¶6, Uncertainties in LOTOS-EUROS); DEPAC-1D as a gap-filling tool is capability_characterized (§5 ¶2); the inadequacy of DEPAC's NH3 pathway parameterization under wet and dry conditions is a contradiction of the model's expected response, kept as an assumption needing investigation (§4.2.1 ¶2); total deposition below critical loads is estimate_with_resolution, supported by cited ecological indicators. Inference: the LOTOS-EUROS runs, including the 2x2 km test, were done by the TNO co-authors; the paper does not say whether the analysis choices (median split thresholds, land-use weighting) were fixed before the comparison. Composition none_fits: the walk is a multi-method intercomparison and model evaluation against an inherited field record, with diagnostic exclusion of rival causes. It is not strong inference (no single crucial test), not capability_first (the capability is inherited), and not independent_replication of a specific published result.

disagreements.target: LOTOS-EUROS v2.0 with the German national (GRETA) emission inventory
disagreements.support: Independent QCL, DELTA and passive-sampler measurements show NH3 overestimated two- to threefold and NOx, not NH3, as the dominant ΣNr compound.
disagreements.quote: A two- to threefold overestimation of NH 3 concentrations by LOTOS-EUROS is visible.

disagreements.target: DEPAC parameterization (expected enhancement of vd under wet, humid, cool conditions)
disagreements.support: Stratified diurnal vd cycles from TRANC show the opposite dependence on RH, leaf wetness and temperature.
disagreements.quote: This behavior was expected based on the models' parameterizations, but it is contradictory to the TRANC measurements.

disagreements.target: Horii et al. (2004) and Thoene et al. (1996) on NO2 non-stomatal deposition and compensation point
disagreements.support: Leaf nitrogen at the site shows no unusual enrichment, so neglecting NO2 emission is argued reasonable for this site.
disagreements.quote: Thus, neglecting the emission pathway of oxidized nitrogen compounds like NO 2 seems reasonable for the measurement site.

disagreements.target: Ahrends et al. (2020) multi-method forest deposition comparison
disagreements.support: Their CBT variant and literature-based inferential method differ from those used here; agreement is limited to their minimum estimates.
disagreements.quote: their CBT was based on the variant suggested by Ulrich (1994), which is different to the version used in this study

disagreements.target: Schrader et al. (2016) on the cuticular NH3 compensation point problem
disagreements.support: Low NH3 levels and monthly averaged emission potentials at the site make the issue an unlikely main cause here.
disagreements.quote: This issue is not solved yet and could not be verified for our measurement site

disagreements.target: van der Graaf et al. (2020) and Ge et al. (2020) model-development attempts
disagreements.support: Satellite LAI/z0 and improved emission timing did not remove the NH3 overestimation over southern Germany or at this site.
disagreements.quote: The attempts of van der Graaf et al. (2020) and Ge et al. (2020) did not provide a solution for the general overestimation

alternatives_considered.alternatives: superimposed synthetic diurnal pattern; monthly averages of half-hours
alternatives_considered.reason: abrupt changes in NH3 (low autocorrelation) could not be reproduced by a synthetic diurnal cycle or monthly half-hourly averages

alternatives_considered.reason: differences in the distribution of vegetation types in the footprint

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Draaijers and Erisman (1995) vs de Vries et al. (2003)

alternatives_considered.reason: no measurements at the EC height; profile started April 2016
